plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies, since your payment (second-highest bid) doesn't depend on your own bid unless you're the winner, and overbidding/underbidding only risks winning at a loss or missing profitable wins. Therefore, the optimal strategy is straightforward: bid exactly my value of $24, ignoring speculation about opponents' beliefs since truthful bidding remains optimal.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do, since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own. Bidding higher than my value risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; bidding lower reduces my chance of winning profitable situations. With a value of $9, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit given the mechanism's incentive structure.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - it doesn't matter what others bid or think about my strategy. If I bid above my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me. If I bid below, I risk losing an item I'd profit from. Therefore, regardless of the other bidders' rationality or beliefs, my optimal action is to bid exactly my true value of $13.
